main_text.p: tias meditabitur capitales, adeoque vindictam quâvis occasione reposcet; quasi non tam per infortunium, quam animo destinato damnum datum fuisse videatur.

Ex parte vero spectatorum non minora evenient incommoda. Ut enim exempla magis movent, quam res aut ratio ipsa, ita illi, qui animosi, qui audaces, spe victoriæ, gloriæ cupiditate, ad illa exercitia incitabuntur: secundum illud Patavini Scriptoris: alios æmulatio & certamen, ut provocarent, provocatiq; ne abnuerent, traxit.Livius histor. libr.28. Alii vero invidia stimulati, quod eum cernant victorem, quem potius victum & superatum optassent, vel secundum cum eodem cogredi desiderabunt quo potius deprimatur, si victus, quam ut obtentâ nuper victoriâ nimiùm elevetur. page.notes: Printed words were transcribed with long s rendered as s. The marginal note "Livius histor. libr.28." is in the left margin, beside the lines of the Patavini quotation; its position within the paragraph is approximate. The last word of the page is "pro-" with a printed hyphen, continued on the next page. The quotation is set in italic and the colon after "Scriptoris" is in roman type. Faint dots and marks at the foot of the page are not printed text and are left out.
